Short Jupyter Tutorial¶

Two types of cells:

  • Code cell (executes python code)
  • Markdown cell (for writing text/LaTex)

New cell: "+" button

Change cell type: Click on "code" at the top and change to "Markdown"

Edit cell: double click

Execute cell: ctrl + enter (or "run" button)

Export .html: File > Download as > HTML

Short LaTex Tutorial¶

Basic Math:

  • This formula $f(x) = x^2$ is an example.
  • $\begin{align*} 1 + 2 &= 3\\ 1 &= 3 - 2 \end{align*}$
  • $f(x) = x^2$
  • $g(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$
  • $F(x) = \int^a_b \frac{1}{3}x^3$
  • $\left[ \begin{matrix} 1 & 0\\ 0 & 1 \end{matrix} \right]$
  • $\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right)$

list_2 = list_1.copy() # shallow copy

# Let's modify list_2

In [12]:
from copy import deepcopy
x = [1, 0]
list_1 = [0, 1, x]
list_2 = deepcopy(list_1)
list_2[2][0] = -10
print(list_1) # [0, 1, [1, 0]]
print(list_2) # [0, 1, [-10, 0]]
print(x) # [1, 0]
# !!! deepcopy is very slow, do not over use it

[0, 1, [1, 0]]
[0, 1, [-10, 0]]
[1, 0]

In [24]:
# accessing the first row
arr_1 = np.array([[0, 1, 2, 3],
[1, 2, 3, 4],
[3, 4, 5, 6]])

# passing "start":"end"
row_0 = arr_1[0, 0:4] # [0, 1, 2, 3]

# we can drop the "start" index
row_0 = arr_1[0, :4] # [0, 1, 2, 3]

# we can drop the "end" index
row_0 = arr_1[0, 0:] # [0, 1, 2, 3]

# we can drop both "start" and "end"
# this is the least verbose way
row_0 = arr_1[0, :] # [0, 1, 2, 3]


# it is possible to use negative indices
arr_1 = np.array([[0, 1, 2, 3],
[1, 2, 3, 4],
[3, 4, 5, 6]])


sub_array = arr_1[0, :-1]

# is equivalent to
sub_array = arr_1[0, :3]
sub_array = arr_1[0:3, -3:-1]

# is equivalent to
sub_array = arr_1[0:3, 1:3]

arr_1 = np.random.rand(3, 2)
arr_2 = np.random.rand(3, 2)
# element wise addition similar to subtraction & division

# Element-wise multiply
arr_3 = np.multiply(arr_1, arr_2)
arr_3 = arr_1 * arr_2 # same as np.multiply()

# matrix mltiplication
arr_4 = np.dot(arr_1, arr_2.T)

# inner product for 1d arrays
arr_4 = np.dot([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3])

plt.plot(x, log2_v)

plt.ylabel('y axis label')
plt.title('log base 2 and 10')
plt.legend(['log10', 'log2'])
plt.show() # next slide

# sub plots
x = np.linspace(1, 4, 15)
log10_v = np.log10(x)
log2_v = np.log2(x)
# one row two cols
# activate plot 1
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)

# plot sub plot 1
plt.plot(x, log10_v)
plt.title('log10')

# activate plot 2
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
# plot sub plot 2
plt.plot(x, log2_v)
plt.title('log2')
plt.show()
